name: cardgame-sync-cards-to-jaina-live
title: Live Jaina card sync — replace the --live stub with a mocked-upsert path
pitch: Extend tools/sync-cards-to-jaina.js so --live actually upserts card records to Jaina through an injectable, mockable client, replacing today's exit-1 'not yet implemented' stub.
why_now: T17 explicitly directed the Producer to re-file this exact live-sync step once cardgame-jaina-card-sync-dryrun merged and specced it as an extension of the existing tool rather than a competing script; the dry-run path (18 cards, slugify parity, byte-identical reruns) already merged and shipped, so the stub is the only piece left unfinished.
expected_outcome: `JAINA_API_URL=... JAINA_API_KEY=... node tools/sync-cards-to-jaina.js --live` exits 0 and prints one upsert result per card; `npm test` proves this against a mocked HTTP client with zero real outbound network calls.
intent: tools/sync-cards-to-jaina.js currently only supports --dry-run (print-only preview) and exits 1 with a 'not yet implemented' message for any other invocation, per the scope decision in T17 that sequenced dry-run before live writes. This unit implements the --live path: for every card record already produced by the existing loadAllCards()/buildRecord() pipeline, perform one upsert against Jaina through an injectable HTTP client so tests can substitute a mock and never touch the real network. This is a content-authoring/sync tool, not gameplay software, so it stays inside the T16 bright line; it handles a live API credential (JAINA_API_KEY) and performs real external writes when actually run, which is why this unit carries the security risk class and should default to a Validate gate.

criteria.text: Given JAINA_API_URL and JAINA_API_KEY env vars and a mocked HTTP client, `node tools/sync-cards-to-jaina.js --live` performs one upsert request per card under design/cards/, using the same record shape (name, slug, costLine, typeLine, rulesText, statsLine) that --dry-run already prints.
The upsert client is injectable/mockable (e.g. an exported function or overridable module), so `npm test` never makes a real network call while still exercising the --live path.

--dry-run keeps its existing exit-0, print-only, no-upsert behavior unchanged — the pre-existing AC1/AC2/AC4 tests in test/sync-cards-to-jaina.test.js still pass without modification to their assertions.
If a mocked upsert rejects or returns a non-2xx status for any card, the script prints which card failed to stderr and exits non-zero rather than silently reporting success for that card.

veto_reason: Duplicate of ms4l0xre-cardgame-jaina-card-sync-live (the canonical live-sync step, correctly filed as security-risk since it writes to RouterBox's real Jaina account).
